record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the knowledge-base exchange community build an iBench-like metadata or exchange-scenario generator for evaluating knowledge-base mapping generation tools, with parameters that control factors such as value invention, incomplete source and target knowledge bases, incomplete correspondences, cycles, and multiple alternative interpretations of a correspondence?

evidence.quote: However, these parameters are not as extensive as the iBench parameters and do not control important factors such as the use of value invention and the number of alternative interpretations for a correspondence.

To begin to address this, we recently proposed a new set of scenarios for KB exchange that covers settings that require value invention, incomplete source and target KBs, incomplete correspondences, and KBs containing cycles [33], though notably our work does not go as far as providing the KB equivalent of an iBench metadata (exchange scenario) generator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Design and construct a parameterized metadata/scenario generator for the evaluation of knowledge-base (KB) mapping generation tools, analogous in spirit to the iBench integration metadata generator used for relational schema mapping benchmarks. Specifically, produce a system that, given a user-supplied configuration, synthesizes complete KB exchange scenarios consisting of: (i) a source KB schema (e.g., a TBox in a description logic or ontology language) together with optional source data (ABox), (ii) a target KB schema together with optional target data, (iii) a set of correspondences/mappings between source and target, and (iv) any auxiliary constraints needed to define the exchange problem. The generator must expose tunable parameters that control at least the following factors:

1. Value invention — the extent to which the target schema requires the introduction of fresh existentially quantified individuals (labeled nulls / Skolem terms) not present in the source.
2. Incompleteness of the source KB — controlled gaps or missing assertions in the source ABox/TBox.
3. Incompleteness of the target KB — controlled gaps or missing assertions in the target ABox/TBox.
4. Incompleteness of correspondences — partial or missing mappings between source and target vocabulary.
5. Presence of cycles in the KBs and/or in the mapping dependency structure.
6. Multiplicity of alternative interpretations of a single correspondence (e.g., the number of semantically distinct logical formalizations a correspondence may admit).

The generator should be capable of producing scenarios of arbitrary size and complexity by composing primitive scenario patterns, and should support repeatable, configurable benchmarking of KB mapping generation tools across all of the above dimensions. The task is to determine whether such a generator can be built and to provide its design and implementation.
artifact.status_search_result: While iBench exists as a mature metadata/scenario generator for relational schema-mapping benchmarks, public searches do not reveal an analogous generator for knowledge-base exchange scenarios that exposes parameters for value invention, incompleteness in source/target KBs and correspondences, cycles, and multiple alternative interpretations of correspondences. Existing KB-exchange scenario collections are more limited in parameter coverage. The challenge therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The iBench Integration Metadata Generator
status_evidence.snippet: iBench generates schemas, constraints, and mappings for relational integration benchmarks with controllable parameters.
status_evidence.claim: iBench addresses the relational schema-mapping benchmarking problem but does not target knowledge-base exchange.

status_evidence.title: iBench GitHub repository
status_evidence.snippet: iBench is a metadata generator for creating arbitrarily large and complex mappings, schemas and constraints.
status_evidence.claim: No analogous KB-exchange generator is offered by the iBench project.

status_evidence.title: ChaseBench
status_evidence.snippet: Benchmark for chase-based data exchange, focused on relational/existential rules scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Related benchmarks exist but do not provide an iBench-style parameterized KB-exchange scenario generator covering value invention, incompleteness, cycles, and multiple correspondence interpretations.
